reason: The typographic observation is half right and everything built on top of it is wrong. Measured in the browser at file://.../lately.html?v=light&state=<state>: .coverage is 11px Geist Mono, letter-spacing 0.99px (0.09em), line-height 14.85px, uppercase, colour #71717a - the voice is as described, and the lab clause is 135 characters, wrapping to four lines (59px) at 390 and two lines (30px) at 768. That much stands. The rest does not. (1) The character counts are inflated: the seat claims the block carries 246-267 characters across states; measured it is 214-235 (full 226, partial 232, quiet 226, first-run 226, empty 235, loading 214, error 223). (2) The 133px is the whole strip - four one-line source stamps plus the clause - not 'a 133px-tall paragraph'; the paragraph is 59px. The complaint is stated at 2.25x its actual size. (3) The load-bearing claim is misattributed. The seat calls this 'the surface's own honesty statement, and the thing a sceptical owner would look for'. It is not. The product's honesty disclosure is the protected 'What this can't tell you' movement, the honest-degradation contract, and the four source stamps that precede this clause (TASKS ANSWERED, TIMELINE ANSWERED, NOTES ANSWERED FOR YOU, READ 09:14...) - each 14-33 characters, one line each, which the seat itself concedes are correctly set. The clause it objects to reads 'weekly counts and ages are lab-authored; Harbour House weddings, Orla, the reading date and the 9 are bound to the shipping fixture' - that is lab-fixture provenance addressed to this panel, naming which numbers were authored for the design lab. A venue owner never reads it, because in the shipped product no numbers are lab-authored. With the false consequence removed, what is left is lab furniture wrapping at two of ten frames - the audit gate already carves out exactly this category (.tl-caption and clip-path furniture are excluded from the letterfit ladder); this string simply is not tagged as furniture. That is a refinement, not a defect. (4) The proposed fix is measurably worse and I drove it to confirm. .t-small sets size, leading and tracking but NOT font-family, and the span sits inside .coverage.t-label which sets font-family: 'Geist Mono'; font-family inherits. Applying the fix verbatim yields computed 13px "Geist Mono" - still mono, now 2px LARGER than the four product source stamps beside it, so the least important string on the surface becomes the largest text in the strip and the hierarchy inverts. And the strip grows at every breakpoint, not shrinks: 133 -> 154px at 390, 84 -> 95px at 768, 51 -> 76px at 1440, because flex:1 1 100% forces its own row where the clause currently sits inline as a single 15px line on desktop, and max-width:68ch at 13px mono is 530px, which wraps it to two 20.15px lines. Seven of the ten named frames are 768 or wider; the fix damages all of them to address a 390-only wrap. 'dim' is also a no-op - .coverage is already color: var(--ink-3) and .dim is var(--ink-3). A correct problem with a wrong fix is refuted, and here the problem is also overstated and mis-consequenced.
sharpenedFix: The voice is not the fault; the string length is. Do not split the strip into two type roles - that invents a Geist Mono|13|small bucket that exists nowhere else in a system which deliberately declares three roles below 15px, and it makes the strip taller on every breakpoint. Instead shorten the clause to stamp length so it obeys the voice it is already set in, and move the fixture-binding detail to plan.html where the panel actually reads it: in shell()'s .coverage block replace the last span's text with 'Lab counts and ages are lab-authored' (38 characters, one line at 768 and up, two at 390), and record the full binding - workspace, owner, reading date, the shared 9 - in the lab's plan.html provenance section. This keeps one voice, one size, one entry on the leading and tracking ladders, holds the strip at 51px on desktop, and touches nothing either gate measures. If the clause must stay in full, tag it as lab furniture the way the gate already recognises furniture rather than giving it a new type role.
breaks: The seat's fix, if landed: inverts the strip's hierarchy (13px mono clause set larger than the 11px product source stamps); adds a Geist Mono|13|small key to the audit gate's family|size|role leading and letterfit maps, a one-instance typographic object; grows .coverage by 21px at 390, 11px at 768 and 25px at 1440, pushing every full-page frame's footer and invalidating all ten shots; and leaves the string in mono anyway because .t-small never overrides font-family. My sharpened fix changes only a text string plus a lab document, so nothing structural moves. After either change re-run audit.mjs --lab=... (type ramp, leading, letterfit, and the AA contrast check on #71717a over the composited paper) and interaction-check.mjs, and re-capture all ten frames - the strip is the last block on the page in every state, so its height shifts total document height and therefore the full-page captures at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440.
